tag-comment.comment: Block comment: {{/* ... */}} — kept distinct from tag bodies so the comment text doesn't get tokenised as keywords/strings.
tag-comment.name: comment.block.squiggly

tag.comment: Any {{ ... }} tag — including the trim variants {{- ... -}}. Inside, all the squiggly tokens come from the #tag-body repository. The `meta.embedded.squiggly` scope on the body shadows whatever the surrounding context was (e.g. an HTML attribute string), so an un-styleable bare identifier doesn't accidentally inherit `hl-string` from `<a href="{{ relURL '/' }}">`-style usage.
tag.name: meta.embedded.squiggly

line-comment.comment: Inline tag-local comment: {{ // ... }} — squiggly's TagParser routes this to a CommentAST.
line-comment.name: comment.line.double-slash.squiggly

single-string.comment: Single-quoted string with C-style escapes — squiggly's TagLexer accepts both single and double quotes for ordinary strings (see the `(elem('\'') | '"')` opener), and they're the conventional choice for inline regex patterns since the regex itself often contains double-quotes. Without this rule, `'\b\w+'` falls through to the bare-token rules and `^`, `[`, `+`, `\` light up as operators or punctuation inside the regex literal.
single-string.name: string.quoted.single.squiggly

raw-string.comment: Backtick-quoted raw string — no escape processing.
raw-string.name: string.quoted.other.squiggly

keyword.comment: Block-control keywords from squiggly's reserved list.
keyword.name: keyword.control.squiggly

operator-word.comment: Word-form operators that share the reserved list with keywords.
operator-word.name: keyword.operator.word.squiggly

assignment.comment: Variable declaration / assignment: $x := expr or $x = expr.

dot-path.comment: Context dot-path: .foo, .foo.bar, or bare . (the cursor). The leading dot lights up as punctuation; the names get the variable scope so themes treat them like fields.

function-call.comment: Identifier immediately followed by '(' is the call form for built-ins (printf, len, slice, ...).

pipe.comment: Pipeline operator. After this, the next identifier is typically a built-in fed by the previous expression.
pipe.name: keyword.operator.pipe.squiggly

operator.comment: Symbolic operators: arithmetic, comparison, range. Order matters — multi-char first so '<=' doesn't tokenise as '<' '='.
operator.name: keyword.operator.squiggly

punctuation.comment: Brackets, parens, comma, colon — kept low-priority so themes can mute them.
punctuation.name: punctuation.squiggly

html-comment.comment: HTML comment block — squiggly never appears inside, by spec.
html-comment.name: comment.block.html

html-doctype.comment: DOCTYPE declaration — typically the first non-blank line of an HTML template. Captures the punctuation, the DOCTYPE keyword itself, and the root element name separately so they each pick up a sensible scope (meta.* would map to no class via scopeCategory and the whole line would render bare).

html-tag.comment: HTML opening, closing, or self-closing tag. The body is a sequence of attributes; squiggly islands are allowed between attributes (handy for {{ if .x }}attr{{ end }} kinds of patterns).

patterns.comment: Attribute name immediately followed by `=`. Boolean attributes (no `=`) are matched by html-attribute-name below.

html-attribute-value-dq.comment: Double-quoted attribute value. Squiggly tags inside (`href="{{ relURL '/' }}"`) are common and must highlight as squiggly, not as plain string.
html-attribute-value-dq.name: string.quoted.double.html

html-attribute-value-bare.comment: Unquoted attribute value (legacy HTML). Stops at whitespace or `>`.
html-attribute-value-bare.name: string.unquoted.html

html-entity.comment: Named, decimal, or hex character reference: &,  ,  .
html-entity.name: constant.character.entity.html
